EUR/USD.paragraph: Spot closed at 1.1395, trading below its SMA20 of 1.1539, SMA50 of 1.1538, and SMA200 of 1.1625. The quote currency retains a 144bp OIS carry advantage, while leveraged funds hold a 37.3% long posture, placing positioning at the 27th percentile of its 52-week range. The broader USD backdrop reflects a 5-day nominal move in the US 5Y yield of +25bp, decomposed into a +24bp rise in real yields and a +1bp shift in breakevens to reach 5.03% nominal (2.70% real, 2.33% breakeven), characterized as real-yield-led. A sustained break back above the 1.1538/1.1539 SMA cluster would neutralize the current downward pressure, whereas failure to reclaim those averages leaves the pair exposed to further downside.

GBP/USD.paragraph: The pair closed at 1.3245, positioned below its SMA20 of 1.344, SMA50 of 1.3466, and SMA200 of 1.3452. AUD/USD.paragraph: The pair closed at 0.7028, trading below its SMA20 of 0.7141 and SMA50 of 0.7096, but holding above its SMA200 of 0.7026. The base currency carries an OIS differential advantage of 47bp, while leveraged funds are positioned 74.5% long, representing the 95th percentile of their 52-week range. A hawkish delivery reinforcing that path would support a push back above the SMA50 at 0.7096, whereas any dovish policy communication would trigger an invalidation of the long posture and open a sustained break below the SMA200 at 0.7026.
